text.tspan: pulsar-binning: the approaches, drawn as what the XMAC multiplies for one group of 8 channels

Each cell is one (FFT window, channel) of the station spectra, coloured by its pulse-phase bin (a toy: 8 bins). Black lines: the tensor-core XMAC's 16-window blocks (its MMA sums 16 windows of a channel at once).
Dispersion delays the lower channels, so the bins slant from channel to channel: a 16-window block can hold several bins, and a different set in each channel.
1.5 ms, 128 channels, 128 bins: a bin is 2.9 windows,
adjacent channels 5.7 windows apart: every block mixes bins
a 10% on-pulse window: most blocks hold no on-pulse
500 ms, 128 bins: a bin is 122-977 windows; a subint
covers 5% of the period: long runs, few bins
binned / unbinned XMAC, ms per subint, 10 stations: RTX 2070 SUPER / A100
walks the windows in time, reading both stations' spectra (CUDA cores, FP32)
holds a sum while the bin stays the same; at each change adds it to that bin's
output in global memory. Dispersion: a warp's channels change bin at different
windows, so those adds do not coalesce (18x faster at DM 0).
The reference for the checks, not a candidate.
● a flush to global memory, per output, at every bin change
the copy into shared memory scales each (window, channel) by sqrt|w| of its bin
(FP16); a negative weight's sign goes into the A operand (one XOR a window).
Each 16-window block is classified first: skipped (all weights 0), copied as is
(all 1), scaled, or scaled with signs. Sum over bins = one weighted sum: one pass.
Costs: the classification, the scaling, a few spilled registers (1.04-1.37x).
the gate: hatched blocks (no on-pulse window in any channel) are skipped
the gate does less than the unbinned XMAC:
the weighted XMAC, once per bin, one-hot weights
each pass keeps one bin (weight 1, the rest 0) and skips the 16-window blocks
without it in any of the block's channels.
With dispersion a bin is in many blocks of an 8-channel group, so the passes
barely skip: nbins x the XMAC, nearly. Every pass also classifies every block
(the slow pulsar's empty bins still cost a pass).
the pass for one bin (colour); x nbins passes
sort → permute → the XMAC over the slots
a stable counting sort per channel (bins computed on the fly); per channel group
each bin gets the same slots, padded to 16 (the most windows any channel has);
a permute writes the spectra in slot order (zeros in the padding); the staged
XMAC runs a block per segment of a bin and writes that bin once.
From channel-major spectra (a transpose in the binning; from window-major the
106 windows sorted into 128 slots: each bin a 16-slot block, the same across the group; grey = padding
sort → the XMAC gathering the slots
the same sort and slots, no permuted copy: the XMAC's copy into its stage reads
each slot's window through the slot table (a 16-B index load per channel and
4 slots, then 4-byte loads) from the channel-major spectra in time order.
Saves the permute's pass; with long runs the loads are nearly contiguous, with runs
of 1-3 windows scattered. Also from the usual window-major spectra (gatherwm, no
copy at all): as fast at 1024 channels, up to 2x slower at 128 or at high DM.
the same slots, read where the windows are
the window order kept; each 16-window block split
at the bins it holds (a masked MMA per bin present, per channel), the sums
written to a bin whenever a channel's bin changes.
Writing the sums inside the window loop (the first sorted kernel did) spilled
0.5-1.9 KB of registers; for long runs gather already does the job, and for short
runs it costs a pass per bin present in a block.
dashed: where each channel's MMA would have to split
The gate and scrunched output (any weights, negative too): weights in the stage, one pass: 0.33-1.37x the unbinned XMAC on the 2070, 0.77-1.80x on the A100.
Separate bins: sorted per channel and gathered, from channel-major spectra (the binning's own transpose) or the usual window-major ones: 3-5x on the A100 in every case but one
(on the 2070 the permuted copy wins for short runs, 6.5x against 12x; on the A100 gather wins there too, 6.6x against 7.1x). Bins narrower than a window (1.5 ms,
1024 channels, 128 bins: 14x / 18x) sample rather than resolve the pulse: warn, do not optimise. A pass per bin and the naive port: not for many bins.
The layouts, slowest index first (the last is contiguous)
— what the station kernel writes now; the stage and passes read it (16-B loads of 4 channels x 1 window)
— a channel's windows contiguous: what sorted and gather start from (a transpose in the binning; gatherwm reads window-major)
— each channel's windows in bin order, bins padded to 16 slots, the same slots across a channel group
bins [window][freq][chan] u8; slotWin [freq][chan][slot] window or -1; segs [freq][group][k] = (bin, first, last + 1 slot block, the bin's segments)
— float2; summed in the XMAC over avg channels, added over an integration with --accumulate

Ratios: run-bins.sh, commit fafcd29: results-local/ar313-adeller-bins-20261122-140307 (2070) and gina8-bins-20261122-142203 (A100, job 21374617); each version's ms per 25.6 ms subint over the unbinned staged XMAC's (2070 1.19-1.50 ms, A100 0.32-0.40);
sorted counts the sort, permute and XMAC, not the channel-major spectra (as a transpose here: 1.4-1.5 ms on the 2070).
